requirement:
Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST explain distributed requirements under
{cite}`requirements.references.distributed`. They MUST direct agents to make a
requirement distributed only when its obligation applies on its own at each of
many sites, such as a convention every validation function follows, and to use
`{impl}` instead when particular code carries out the requirement as a whole, and
to mark with `{impl}` the code that carries out any obligation of a distributed
requirement that its sites do not uphold. They
MUST direct agents to write site queries that select every place the obligation
applies and no others, violation queries for every kind of construct that could
break it, and
`match` and `no_match` snippets for every query that include near misses. They
MUST direct agents to describe sites exactly as the site queries select them,
stating as an obligation any convention the queries rely on, such as how a list
is named, and to state only per-site obligations that a reviewer can check at the
site and the helpers it calls. They MUST direct agents to
present the queries with the requirement text when reviewing the requirement with
the user. They MUST tell agents that sites need no reference to the requirement,
that `habeas author --all` authors site reviews under
{cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, and that a false site review is
addressed by fixing the site, or by tightening the queries or the requirement
text when the site should not be covered or the text admits more than one
reading, under {cite}`requirements.cli.flip_guidance`, not by re-running the
review. The requirements skill MUST give this guidance as a list of things to do and
things not to do. The bootstrap skill MUST direct agents to propose a distributed
requirement for a cross-cutting convention instead of marking each of its sites
with `{impl}`.
rationale:
**Content.** The bundled skills carry nearly every directive in the requirement. The gap is in the test.

**Where each obligation is met:**
- **Explain distributed requirements:** `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/references/distributed-requirements.md` does this in its intro and its "Queries" section, which gives the query kinds, the keys, a worked example and how sites are chosen.
- **Distributed only when the obligation applies at each site, `{impl}` otherwise:** first "Do" item.
- **Mark with `{impl}` the code that carries out an obligation the sites do not uphold:** third "Do" item. The third "Don't" item also covers it.
- **Site queries select every place and no others:** the "Before review, check…" item.
- **Violation queries for every kind of construct:** the "Write a violation query…" item.
- **`match` and `no_match` snippets with near misses:** the "Give every query a `match` snippet…" item.
- **Describe sites exactly as queried and state the convention:** the "Describe sites exactly…" item, plus the first "Don't".
- **Per-site obligations a reviewer can check:** the second "Don't".
- **Present the queries with the requirement text:** a "Do" item. Step 3 of `habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` says the same.
- **Sites need no reference:** the third "Don't".
- **`habeas author --all` authors site reviews:** the "Review" section and the last "Do" item.
- **False site review handled by fixing the site or tightening the queries or text, not by re-running:** the "Site reviews" section of `habeas-evidence/SKILL.md`, plus the last "Don't".
- **Requirements skill gives this guidance as do and don't lists:** the "Do" and "Don't" headings in the reference file.
- **Bootstrap skill proposes a distributed requirement for a cross-cutting convention:** `habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md`, in the paragraph "When a convention applies on its own at many sites…".

**Test gap.** The only `{test}` is `bundled_skills_guide_distributed_requirements_with_do_and_dont_lists` in `tests/authoring_cli.rs`. It asserts the Do and Don't phrases, the `habeas author --all` sentence in the requirements skill, three phrases in `habeas-evidence`, and one in the bootstrap skill. Two obligations are never asserted:
1. **Explain distributed requirements under `requirements.references.distributed`.** Nothing checks the "Queries" section or the explanation of sites and query kinds. This obligation is not exempt, because checking it means checking that text is present.
2. **Fix by tightening the text when it "admits more than one reading".** The test asserts only the "narrow the site query or tighten the text describing sites" sentence in `habeas-evidence`. It does not assert the "if the obligation's text admits a reading under which the site fails, tighten that text" clause.

The other tests that mention the reference file (`bundled_skills_open_with_a_workflow_and_name_their_neighbors` and `bundled_skill`) carry no `{test}` reference to this requirement. They also do not check these points.

Because these obligations have no asserting test, I judge the requirement not satisfied. I found no `{fixme}` acknowledging the gap.

text: :::{req} distributed_guidance
Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST explain distributed requirements under
{cite}`requirements.references.distributed`. They MUST direct agents to make a
requirement distributed only when its obligation applies on its own at each of
many sites, such as a convention every validation function follows, and to use
`{impl}` instead when particular code carries out the requirement as a whole, and
to mark with `{impl}` the code that carries out any obligation of a distributed
requirement that its sites do not uphold. They
MUST direct agents to write site queries that select every place the obligation
applies and no others, violation queries for every kind of construct that could
break it, and
`match` and `no_match` snippets for every query that include near misses. They
MUST direct agents to describe sites exactly as the site queries select them,
stating as an obligation any convention the queries rely on, such as how a list
is named, and to state only per-site obligations that a reviewer can check at the
site and the helpers it calls. They MUST direct agents to
present the queries with the requirement text when reviewing the requirement with
the user. They MUST tell agents that sites need no reference to the requirement,
that `habeas author --all` authors site reviews under
{cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, and that a false site review is
addressed by fixing the site, or by tightening the queries or the requirement
text when the site should not be covered or the text admits more than one
reading, under {cite}`requirements.cli.flip_guidance`, not by re-running the
review. The requirements skill MUST give this guidance as a list of things to do and
things not to do. The bootstrap skill MUST direct agents to propose a distributed
requirement for a cross-cutting convention instead of marking each of its sites
with `{impl}`.
:::{req} distributed
A requirement MAY be distributed: it states obligations that each of many sites
in the sources must uphold on its own, such as a convention every validation
function follows, and MAY also state obligations that particular code carries
out, which that code implements with `{impl}`. A `{req}` body declares a distributed requirement
by containing one or more nested query directives: `:::{sites} <name>` for a
site query, which finds the places the obligation applies, or
`:::{violations} <name>` for a violation query, which finds constructs likely to
break it. A requirement with a violation query MUST also have a site query.
Query names MUST be single identifier segments under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`, unique within the requirement. A query
directive outside a `{req}` body MUST be a validation error. Each query body
MUST be one fenced `yaml` code block containing a mapping with only these keys:
- `language`, required: the name of an outline profile with a grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines`: `rust`, `python`, `typescript`,
`tsx`, `css`, `markdown`, `toml`, or `yaml`.
- `paths`, optional: project-relative files or directories. Only sources at or
under one of them are searched; without it, every source of the language is.
- `exclude`, optional: project-relative files or directories whose sources are
not searched, even under `paths`.
- `rule`, required, with optional `utils` and `constraints`: an ast-grep rule
core in the syntax of Habeas's pinned `ast-grep-config` version, matched
against the language's pinned grammar.
- `within`, required for violation queries and not allowed for site queries:
the name of a site query in the same requirement.
- `match` and `no_match`, required: nonempty lists of source snippets in the
query's language. Each `match` snippet MUST contain at least one match of the
query, and each `no_match` snippet none, where a violation query counts only matches inside a site of its `within` query in the same snippet.
Validation MUST report a query whose body is not such a mapping, whose rule does
not compile, whose `within` names no site query of the requirement, a violation query without `within`, or one of whose snippets fails to parse or has the wrong match result, and a site query
that matches nothing in the project. Queries MUST search exactly the sources
reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, in
their original text.
A match's site MUST be the innermost outline node, under

{cite}`requirements.references.outlines`, whose range contains the match; for a violation query, it MUST instead be the innermost site of its `within` query that contains the match, and a match inside none of that query's
sites MUST be discarded. A requirement's sites MUST be the distinct sites of all
its queries' matches. Each site MUST have a site review under
{cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, and needs no reference to the
requirement; being a site MUST NOT count as a reference for
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, because a distributed
requirement concerns a cross-cutting obligation, not why the item exists.
Upgrading `ast-grep-config` MAY change matches and MUST be treated as a
deliberate change. The book MUST render each query directive as a badge
naming its kind and name, followed by its code block.
:::{req} site_review
Every site of a distributed requirement under
{cite}`requirements.references.distributed` MUST have a site review: an
assessment of whether that site upholds the requirement, recorded at
`evidence/sites/<full-name>/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` and
`<selector>` are encoded as under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. The review MUST use the prompt
defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.site_prompt`. Mandatory inputs, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the site's outline
node, the requirement's complete declaration, and each declaration the
requirement cites. The record MUST contain the requirement's full name, the
site's file and selector, `queries`, the sorted names of the queries with a
match at the site, `applies`, `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`, with
determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. `applies` MUST be a
Boolean recording whether the requirement applies to the site. A site to which
the requirement does not apply MUST be judged `true`, and the rationale MUST
explain why it does not apply. `habeas info` MUST report, for each selected
distributed requirement, how many of its sites the requirement does not apply
to.
Validation MUST require a current, accepted review for every site, MUST report a
false review with its rationale, and MUST report stale, missing, or orphaned
reviews; a review is orphaned when its file and selector no longer name a site
of the requirement. A `{fixme}` naming the requirement inside a site
acknowledges a gap at that site only: it MUST be an input to that site's review
and MUST NOT contribute to the requirement's own review, coverage, or reference
set. A review MUST become stale when the site's hash, the requirement's
declaration, a cited declaration, its `queries`, or the `{fixme}` references
naming the requirement inside the site, with the words of their bodies, change.
Each site review's determination MUST be checked on its own, independently of
the requirement's evidence. Authoring with `--all` MUST include site reviews,
`habeas author sites:<full-name>` MUST author the site reviews of the named
requirement, and `habeas author sites:<full-name>/<file>#<selector>` MUST author
the review of the one site it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>` names the
file's root node. `habeas status` MUST report missing, stale, invalid, and false
site reviews with their requirement, file, and selector, and `habeas info` MUST
list each selected requirement's sites with their determinations.
:::{req} flip_guidance
Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST state the goal that independent assessments
of the same subject reach the same determination, because the requirement, code,
and tests leave no gap a careful reviewer could find and no reading a careful
reviewer could take differently. They MUST tell agents that assessments of the
same subject that disagree are findings against that goal. They MUST direct agents to read both
rationales and decide whether one assessment found a real gap or the requirement
text admits more than one reading, then fix the source or tests, or tighten the
requirement text, rather than re-running an assessment to obtain a different
determination. Every change to agreed requirement text, including a rewording for precision,
MUST be reviewed with the user under
{cite}`requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill` before it is made, and the
skills MUST then direct agents to record the old text, new text, reason, and the
rationale that prompted the change in the project's audit log, such as
`audits/requirement-rewordings/`.
